– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The `BZip2CompressorInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)` method implementation is responsible for reading bytes from the compressed input stream into the destination buffer. In this method, the loop reads bytes from the stream until either the buffer is filled or the stream is finished. If the buffer is filled, the number of bytes read is returned; otherwise, -1 is returned to indicate the end of the stream.

From the failing test case and the bug report, it seems that there is an issue with the return value of `BZip2CompressorInputStream.read` when it is instructed to read to a full buffer. The report mentions that the method returns -1 when given an offset equal to the length of the buffer, which can be misinterpreted as the stream being finished rather than the buffer being full.

To locate the fault, we need to analyze how the return value is determined in the `read` method and whether there is a specific condition causing -1 to be returned when the buffer is full.

Let's proceed with the diagnosis to understand the root cause of this issue.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The `BZip2CompressorInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)` method is designed to read bytes from the compressed input stream into the destination buffer. The method iterates over the input stream, filling the destination buffer until the buffer is full or the stream is finished. If the buffer is filled, the method returns the number of bytes read; otherwise, it returns -1 to indicate the end of the stream.

The bug report indicates that when the offset provided to the `read` method is equal to the length of the buffer, the method returns -1. This behavior can be misleading because it may imply that the stream has ended when, in fact, the buffer is full. 

Looking at the code snippet of the `BZip2CompressorInputStream.read` method, we can see that the condition for determining the return value is based on `destOffs`, which is the index tracking the current position in the destination buffer. If `destOffs` remains equal to `offs` (the provided offset), -1 is returned to signal that no bytes were read into the buffer.

To address this issue, we need to adjust the logic in the `read` method to ensure that when the buffer is full, the return value reflects the number of bytes read instead of -1. This adjustment will provide a more accurate indication to the caller regarding the status of the read operation.

Given the situation, the following method should be fixed:
`org.apache.commons.compress.compressors.bzip2.BZip2CompressorInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
